title: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision + Outlook Report (MPM Jan 21-22, 2027)
source: NEWS: boj.or.jp 'Monetary Policy Meetings' schedule page (en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/), fetched raw (HTTP 200, 41,959 bytes) and column-parsed out of the HTML direct 2026-09-05. The page carries TWO tables — 'Table : 2026' and 'Table : 2027' — with columns 'Date of MPM | Outlook Report (The Bank's View) | Summary of Opinions | MPM Minutes'; the 2027 table's first row reads 'Jan. 21 (Thurs.), 22 (Fri.)' with 'Jan. 22 (Fri.)' in the Outlook Report column, 'Feb. 1 (Mon.)' for the Summary of Opinions and 'Mar. 24 (Wed.)' for the Minutes. The decision publishes at the meeting's conclusion on the second day. THIS IS an Outlook Report meeting, unlike December 2026. Filed estimate on three counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: and no slot for any other central bank, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and a schedule published ~16 months ahead is the most movable kind. Understating the label only widens caution.
notes: Proposed during the boj-decision-2026-12-18 initial research (2026-09-05) as the next venue after that decision, and the meeting that inherits the pace question if December disappoints. SAME CHANNEL, SAME CAVEAT AS THE THREE 2026 BoJ ENTRIES: a BoJ move propagates to this calendar's long-duration AI names through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order for a US equity book and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers; symbols is empty and no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed. IMPACT IS MEDIUM for the same reason as the sibling BoJ entries. Policy rate is 1.0% as of the 2026-07-31 statement (8-1, Takata dissenting for 1.25% — confirmed by his own 2026-09-02 Sapporo speech, boj.or.jp/en/about/press/koen_2026/data/ko260902a1.pdf: 'At the July MPM, I proposed that the Bank raise the policy interest rate to 1.25 percent'). WHY THIS ONE MATTERS BEYOND BEING NEXT: it is an Outlook Report meeting, so it carries the fresh staff projections December cannot, and it is the first BoJ meeting of the year the surveys point at for the move to 1.50% — Reuters' 2026-07-23 poll (FXStreet syndication) found '70% of economists anticipate the BoJ to hike rates to at least 1.50% in Q2 of 2027, while 51% of respondents see 1.50% as the terminal rate'. The decision announcement lands overnight ET and reaches the US tape as a 01-22 open. Date is the JST decision date, matching how the BoJ publishes it. Adjacent on this calendar as of 2026-09-05: fomc-2027-01-27 five days later.
